Subject: Order form redline: downstream product rights & evidence checklist

Danielle —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Per our discussion I’m sending over the current Order Form + MSA redline items we expect will come up so we can line up on the path to sign. Main areas we want to resolve quickly:

- Output ownership / productization carveouts (BrightCom has asked for explicit downstream product rights)
- Training/data use & telemetry (what consents are needed for model improvement, telemetry retention)
- Feedback / evaluation license (how customer-provided feedback may be used for product quality)

I’ve attached an evidence checklist we’ll need if BrightCom requires any expanded rights (proof of data provenance, access controls, PII sanitization steps). Can you confirm your legal team’s redlines and any non-starter asks? If possible let’s aim to exchange markups by EOD Wed so we can keep procurement timelines intact.

Proposed next steps:
1) You send BrightCom’s redlines (MSA + Order Form)
2) We return redline with limited carveouts + suggested operational controls (retention, opt-out for retraining)
3) If there are any productization exclusivity asks we’ll raise to GTM/legal and provide a counterproposal with time-bound evidence/escrow options

Thanks — I’ll loop in legal and CS for wording and handoff.

—Sean

Sean —

Thanks for the note and checklist. I’ve attached our redlines to the MSA and the draft Order Form for your review (BrightCom_MSA_redlines.docx). High-level asks from our side:

- We need explicit downstream productization rights for outputs when BrightCom provides content or fine-tuning data; we see this as necessary for our roadmap.
- We want a "training consent" default that covers improvements to models used by BrightCom; we’ll accept a limited opt‑out but want clear notice periods.
- Feedback license: we’d like non-exclusive license to use anonymized model outputs/feedback internally and with partners.

A couple of clarifying questions for Redwood:
1) If we give broader output rights, what operational safeguards can you provide around PII and telemetry retention?
2) Can Redwood provide evidence (logs or certificate) showing customer data is not used outside scoped retraining?
3) Would Redwood consider a commercial carveout (time-bound) rather than an open-ended assignment?

I’ve looped in Markus from our legal team for any technical/legal follow-ups. We’re trying to keep this within our Q2 procurement window — happy to set a short working session Wed afternoon.

Thanks,
Danielle
Danielle Park | Head of Platform Partnerships
BrightCom

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Order form redline: downstream product rights & evidence checklist

Team —

Reviewed BrightCom’s redlines. High level guidance and recommended counter language below. I attached a marked-up response (Redwood_response_markups.docx) and a quick snapshot for the exec read (redline_snapshot.pdf).

Summary of recommended positions:
1) Output/productization: counter with a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable license to use outputs for BrightCom’s internal productization, subject to strict scope: (i) explicitly exclude rights to embed Redwood models into a competing SaaS; (ii) require documented provenance and customer-provided data flags.

Proposed clause (short): "Customer may use Outputs to develop or improve Customer Products solely for Customer's internal business purposes; any broader commercialization requires express written consent from Redwood."

2) Training / telemetry: accept a scoped training consent but implement an explicit opt‑out and operational controls: 
- Data flagged as "no-train" must be excluded from model retraining and any aggregate telemetry used for product improvement;
- Retention windows for telemetry/logs (default 90 days, extendable for support with notice);
- Provide an evidence bundle (audit logs, redacted samples) on reasonable request under an NDA.

3) Feedback license: offer a perpetual, non-exclusive license for anonymized feedback for Redwood to improve services, with an assurance that PII is never retained. If BrightCom needs to use anonymized outputs with partners, include a limited sublicense right for partners working on BrightCom’s behalf only.

Operational asks for Sales/CS: we’ll need the evidence_checklist items completed before we accept broader rights — particularly data provenance and access control attestation. Grace, please own documentation and evidence collection (see attached checklist). Karthik, can you confirm product constraints for any technical exclusivity asks and whether we should offer a time-boxed commercial carveout (e.g., 12 months) instead of open assignment?

I think we can bridge here but we should avoid assignment/transfer language and keep any productization rights narrow and instrumented.

—Laura
Laura Bennett | Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_response_markups.docx; redline_snapshot.pdf

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Danielle Park <danielle.park@brightcom.com>
Cc: BrightCom Legal <legal@brightcom.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Order form redline: downstream product rights & evidence checklist

Danielle / Markus / BrightCom legal —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Per internal review (Laura & product looped) attached is our marked response and an operational checklist we’ll need completed to enable any expanded output/training permissions. Key points we’re proposing:

- Outputs: limited non-exclusive productization license for internal use; explicit prohibition on bundling Redwood models into a competing SaaS; any commercial redistribution requires written approval.
- Training: allow "opt-in" default for BrightCom with a documented opt-out flag; 90-day telemetry retention standard and evidence provision under NDA.
- Feedback: Redwood retains a non-exclusive license to use anonymized feedback for product improvements; BrightCom may permit partners to use anonymized outputs only for BrightCom-authorized integrations.

Attached: Redwood_response_markups.docx, evidence_checklist.xlsx.

Request: If this is acceptable in principle, can BrightCom incorporate the counter-clauses into your next redline pass and we’ll schedule a 30-min legal/ops sync Thurs morning to finalize operational evidence items? If you prefer a commercial carveout instead of an open-ended assignment, we can propose a 12-month time-box in the Order Form.

Next steps:
- BrightCom: confirm which of the three positions (Outputs / Training / Feedback) are non‑negotiable for you; mark any sections as critical changes.
- Redwood: Laura to prepare final clause language for any agreed carveouts; Grace to collect evidence checklist items.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this week if we can align on the small set of items.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher | Account Executive
Redwood Inference
